briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. We will now begin the climate briefing for August 3, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Extreme Heatwaves Domestically and Internationally, and Deepening Climate Variability
sections.content: Today, South Korea recorded a heatwave exceeding 42.5 degrees Celsius for the first time in meteorological observation history, with extreme heat continuing, including the issuance of the first severe heatwave warning in the Seoul metropolitan area [1, 13, 113, 126]. This unprecedented heatwave is estimated to cause 3.6 trillion Korean Won in damages annually in South Korea alone, raising concerns about casualties among vulnerable populations, such as foreign workers falling unconscious due to heatstroke [26, 112]. The global community is also experiencing a 'cruel summer' with extreme weather phenomena such as heat domes in the U.S., droughts and wildfires in Europe, and storms in South America, while the Super El Niño phenomenon is leading to more frequent heatwaves and heavy rainfall [5, 16, 31, 121, 122]. Scientists warn that global heating has entered a dangerous new phase, suggesting an urgent need to redesign climate change standards and response systems to cope with extreme heatwaves that would not have occurred 50 years ago [1, 21, 124].

sections.title: ⚠️ Ecosystem Threats and Widespread Impacts of Climate Change
sections.content: Climate change poses a severe threat to ecosystems, and its impacts are spreading widely. In particular, the Red-banded Hairstreak butterfly (Hongjulnabi) has been designated as an endangered wild species for August due to the decline of pine nut forests and climate change, indicating that the long-standing symbiotic relationship between conifers and butterflies is being severed [3, 6, 12]. Internationally, climate change is threatening crop nutrition and putting New York's power grid to the test [114, 116], with significant repercussions such as increased risks in Himalayan climbing environments and threats to the Camino de Santiago pilgrimage tradition [117, 123]. Amidst these circumstances, Ghana is experiencing flood damage, and countries like Nauru are facing difficulties in securing funds for climate response [30, 120].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic Efforts and Policy Challenges for Achieving Carbon Neutrality
sections.content: Various local governments and institutions in South Korea are actively striving to achieve carbon neutrality. In Gwangmyeong City, the number of citizens participating in the 'Climate Militia' has surpassed 20,000, leading the practice of carbon neutrality in daily life [36, 52, 54, 56, 58, 61, 64, 66, 68, 69, 71, 72], and Daejeon City is reorganizing its forest policies around AI and carbon neutrality to respond to the climate crisis [40, 42, 49, 74, 79]. Jeju National University is actively engaging in industry-academia cooperation, partnering with Korea Midland Power to achieve carbon neutrality and foster future talent [15, 33, 34, 35, 43, 44, 48, 55]. However, there are strong calls to reflect early reduction targets in the Carbon Neutrality Framework Act [39, 57, 75, 76], and the low subscription rate and high loss ratio of climate insurance remain key policy challenges that need to be addressed [29].

sections.title: ⚡ Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition and the Role of Corporations
sections.content: The transition to renewable energy is accelerating in South Korea, in line with global trends. The UN carbon market is expanding into renewable energy sectors such as solar and wind power [80], and new and renewable energy infrastructure is growing, including the groundbreaking of South Korea's largest solar power plant in Haenam [101]. Hanmi Group has initiated its renewable energy transition with the goal of achieving RE100 by 2040 and has signed a Power Purchase Agreement (PPA), while the government's tax reform plan also includes measures to strengthen support for solar power generation [83, 85, 93, 103, 111]. A pilot project for issuing REGOs (Renewable Energy Guarantees of Origin) to help companies use 100% renewable energy is also planned [87], but Meta's withdrawal from RE100 and LG Energy Solution's stagnant transition rate raise concerns about the fulfillment of renewable energy commitments [88, 95].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has highlighted unprecedented extreme weather phenomena, the resulting threats to ecosystems, and the response efforts from various sectors of society. Sustained attention and action are crucial to overcome the climate crisis, and this is a critical time when policy support and international cooperation are urgently needed. This concludes the climate briefing for August 3, 2026.
